newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hugo Boss plans women's clothes.
newsitem.headline: Hugo Boss plans women's clothes.

text.p: Men's fashion retailer Hugo Boss said Monday it planned to broaden its position in the fashion world, preparing to launch a women's collection early next year.
Hugo Boss, which is majority-held by Italy's Marzotto Group, also said it would begin marketing a women's scent, Hugo Woman, as a counterpart to its Hugo fragrance, this August.
"In January 1998 we plan to launch a collection for the fashion conscious woman aged between 20 and 40 years old," the group said in the statement.
Hugo Boss is one of the more popular men's lines in the United States.

Boss has seen strong growth from its decision to split its product lines into three groups from one -- Boss for traditional buyers, Hugo for younger, more contemporary buyers and Baldessarini for top-line customers.

But the company has been hampered by leadership issues after Boss Chief Executive Peter Littmann, 49, left the firm at the start of 1997 after an apparent dispute with Marzotto officials over the direction of the Stuttgart- based group.
Joachim Vogt, a 44-year-old production and logistics executive at Boss, has taken over as management board chairman from Littmann.
